### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/trigger-record-change`, touching **58** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **11** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**80** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd7ea2e355c3829ff1b3da93f046308ee6f6eb16`.

⛔ **18** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **11** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`, `responseSchema (7 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/automation/:name (route, 54 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **184** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd7ea2e355c3829ff1b3da93f046308ee6f6eb16` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2e6540d20ab56429595fea7eba0260e137b26c90` — the merge of head `41487226fa0c4be52fa3085a09e0cd806434b563` into base `cd7ea2e355c3829ff1b3da93f046308ee6f6eb16`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2e6540d20ab56429595fea7eba0260e137b26c90 && git checkout 2e6540d20ab56429595fea7eba0260e137b26c90
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cd7ea2e355c3829ff1b3da93f046308ee6f6eb16 41487226fa0c4be52fa3085a09e0cd806434b563 && git checkout -B drift-repro cd7ea2e355c3829ff1b3da93f046308ee6f6eb16 && git merge --no-ff 41487226fa0c4be52fa3085a09e0cd806434b563

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd7ea2e355c3829ff1b3da93f046308ee6f6eb16
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cd7ea2e355c3829ff1b3da93f046308ee6f6eb16` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `99bfd857eb823d672ab57e10b0c7d916d2064a27`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/index.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/record-change-trigger-events.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/address-grammar.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-address.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/record-update-starts.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/src/record-change-trigger.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/stageChangeStarts.tsx

PR #36316, card #35928, ruling record 7073655354, claim amended 7076933558. Read: the card and all 9 comments, the PR body, the 60-file net diff against base `b3bcfefc`, and the check-runs on the head (64 success, 13 skipped, 1 failure: the first `Check Changeset` run of 09:07Z, superseded by two green runs of 09:08Z and 09:42Z on the same head). The cited code was read in the head tree; nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- `@objectstack/spec/api` gains `RecordUpdateStartsRequestSchema`, `RecordUpdateStartSchema`, `RecordUpdateStartsResponseSchema`, their input and `Parsed` types, and the contract entry `AutomationApiContracts.listRecordUpdateStarts` (`POST /api/v1/automation/_record-starts`). Additive. The generated `api-surface`, `export-origins`, `declaration-map`, `json-schema.manifest` and `authorable-surface` shards carry exactly these 9 exports, 3 schemas and 10 keys, nothing else: right.
- `@objectstack/spec/automation` gains `recordChangeTriggerHookEvents` and `recordChangeTriggerFiresOnUpdate`; the body is the trigger package's former `triggerTypeToHookEvents`, moved unedited, and that export stays and delegates. One grammar, no accept-set change for `triggerType`: right.
- `@objectstack/spec/contracts` gains `RecordUpdateStartsInput` and the OPTIONAL `IAutomationService.listRecordUpdateStarts`. Optional, so no existing implementer breaks; the door answers 501 without it: right.
- `NAMESPACE_POSITION_LITERALS.automation.literals` gains `_record-starts`, in code-unit order ahead of `_status`. `NAMESPACE_PATTERN` and `ROUTER_ADDRESSABLE_NAME_PATTERN` are both letter-led and admit no hyphen, so no namespace and no flow name is newly refused or shadowed, and `NAMESPACE_REFUSED_LITERALS` is unchanged. A qualifier followed by the literal is declined through the derived `AUTOMATION_DOOR_LITERALS`. Widening only: right.
- Accept-set of the request: `object` and `recordId` non-empty strings, `changes` a record of any string key to unknown, strict at the top level. The top level is right. The `changes` key set is too wide: see M1.
- Response: `{ name, label, startsApproval }` per flow and nothing else, as ruled (no description, condition, node or link). `label` is required on `FlowSchema`, so `z.string()` holds for every registered flow: right.
- Route ledger: one row, `disposition: 'sdk'`, `client: 'automation.listRecordUpdateStarts'` (the method exists in `packages/client`), both schema names resolve, census 149 to 150. The note states the gate order the handler has. The envelope schema named in `responseSchema` follows the `POST /automation/:name/clone` row's precedent. The row's `requestSchema` pin is incomplete: see S2.
- Authorisation per caller: the domain-wide anonymous floor answers 401 first; the door is outside `isFlowAuthoringWrite`, so no capability is asked, as ruled ("no new capability"). The record is read through `callData` `get` with the caller's `executionContext`: that passes `refuseUnexposedDataAction` (the object's `apiEnabled` and `apiMethods`, and a disabled package refused), then `protocol.getData` under the caller's permissions, row scope and field masking, which throws `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` for an absent or unreadable row. The engine is reached only after that read. Permission and exposure are both the `/data` door's own, not a second reading: right.
- What the door reveals beyond the record read: flow names and labels of the object's armed update flows. The ruling's premise (a signed-in member already reads every flow label at `/meta/flow`) was measured live by the dev before code; no narrower audience exists to leak past: right.
- `@objectstack/client`: `automation.listRecordUpdateStarts(request)` returns the unwrapped `data`: right.
- `@object-ui/i18n`: `detail.stageChangeStartsHeading` and `detail.stageChangeStartsApproval` are present in all 11 packs (ar, de, en, es, fr, ja, ko, pt-BR, ru, zh-Hans, zh-Hant), inside the `detail` group, and the `en` fallback in `useDetailTranslation.ts` is byte-identical to the `en` pack: right.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/35928-record-update-starts-read.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor; `service-automation`, `trigger-record-change`, `runtime`, `client` patch. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` matches the diff (new exports, one new route, nothing removed or re-typed). `Metadata-protocol: added` is what `Check Changeset` derives from the moved `authorable-surface/api.json` baseline (10 keys), and `added` takes at least minor on the package that moves it: `@objectstack/spec` minor is right. All five packages sit in the one `fixed` group, so the published level is the same either way.
- `.changeset/35928-stage-confirm-names-flows.md`: five `@object-ui/*` packages patch, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. The UI half adds exports and two locale keys and moves no authorable surface; `utils/flowsBundle` was module-internal to `@object-ui/app-shell` (no package export), so its move removes nothing public: right.
- The PR body's `Clause-②: yes (widening ...)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` lines agree with the changesets. The gate verdict is the green `Check Changeset` run on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, approval mark through a `subflow` node (`showcase_project_closure` listed with `startsApproval: false`): answered. The ruling's test is "a flow that contains an approval node"; the code implements exactly that, and the wider reading is filed as #36322.
- Dev flag, overlap with #36296 and #36236: answered, both landed and are merged in. Overlap with #36335 (the same `activeFlowsBundle` move): answered, the later lander drops its copy.
- Dev flag, masked fields: a condition is judged on the record as the caller reads it, so the preview can under-list and never reveals a masked value. Read in the code and true: `previous` and `record` are both built from the caller-scoped read, and a caller-supplied key cannot forge `previous` or `current_user` (both are bound after the flattened record keys). Documented in `flows.mdx`. Answered.
- Declaration correction, `Metadata-protocol: none` in the ruling and the first claim, `added` in the amended claim 7076933558: the three schemas are API request and response shapes, no flow key, no metadata type and no capability is added, so the ruling's "no new capability and no new authorable key" holds as meant. The line itself was changed by the seat, not by the maintainer: escalated below for visibility, not a finding.
- `open_questions` on the latest dev report (7077329380): none.
- SQL push-down (AGENTS.md Prime Directive 5): no finding. The door makes ONE by-id read through the data door; the engine walks its in-process flow registry and reads no table; no id list is materialised and nothing is joined in the app. Each confirm asks once per pending move, not per row.
- Security: a security item is with the owner seat.

### ④ Design judgment

M1 (must-fix) — the door accepts a `changes` key that is not a declared field of `object`. Rule: the door refuses an undeclared key (400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`) before the engine is asked, and the request schema constrains a key to the field-name grammar; a pin sends an undeclared key and asserts the refusal. A security item is with the owner seat.

S1 (should-fix) — the preview is the live gate's function over a narrower context, and the contract says otherwise. `IAutomationService.listRecordUpdateStarts` and `RecordUpdateStartsResponseSchema` say the condition is "evaluated by the ONE start-condition gate a live run passes", and `RecordUpdateStartsInput.userId` says `current_user` is bound "as the record-change trigger forwards the writer on a live save". A live run evaluates the gate on `resolveRunContext`'s result: for the default `runAs: 'user'` flow `seedRunGrants` has resolved the writer's `positions`, so `current_user.positions` and `current_user.isPlatformAdmin` are real; the preview passes only `userId` and `tenantId`, so both read as empty and false although the door holds the caller's positions in its `executionContext`. A condition such as `!current_user.isPlatformAdmin` is listed for an administrator whose save starts nothing (an over-listing, under a heading that says "Saving this change starts these flows"), and a position test is under-listed. Two smaller gaps of the same kind: the trigger hands the record as `params` (so an `isInput` variable named like a field takes the record's value, where the preview keeps its default) and expands the start node's declared `expand` lookups before the gate. Hand the engine the caller's positions (an optional member on `RecordUpdateStartsInput`, additive) and `params`, or state the limits in the two docblocks and `flows.mdx`. Non-blocking: carry on a follow-up card.

S2 (should-fix) — the ledger row fills `requestSchema` without the pin the ledger's own rule requires. `RouteLedgerEntry.requestSchema` says: do not fill a row without a suite that drives this handler, shows each declared member reaching the producer and an undeclared one not reaching it, "and asserts this row names the schema it parses with". `automation-record-update-starts.test.ts` does the first three and not the last; the two precedent rows do (`automation-flow-clone-custom-package.test.ts`, `packages-publish-drafts-request-conformance.test.ts`, each `expect(row.requestSchema).toBe(...)`). One assertion. Non-blocking: carry on a follow-up card, or fold into the M1 push.

N1 (nit) — `respondToRecordUpdateStarts` falls back to `stored = {}` when the read answers without a record, and then judges the flows on `changes` alone. `protocol.getData` and the engine fallback both throw 404 on a miss, so no door reaches it today; a read that returns no record should be refused, not judged.

N2 (nit) — the module note of `automation-address.ts` lists the door's literals in prose twice (`trigger`, `hooks`, `connectors`, `actions`, `_status`) without `_record-starts`; the constant it describes is derived and correct.

Held, sentence by sentence: the request and response docblocks against the handler (order: query set, body, 501, caller-scoped read, engine); the ledger note against the handler; the contract docblock's "enabled, armed, record-change, this object, token binds an update" against `record-update-starts.ts` (`isFlowEnabled`, `boundFlowTriggers`, `resolveTriggerBinding`, `recordChangeTriggerFiresOnUpdate`); "a condition that cannot be evaluated is not listed" (the catch); "hooks are never listed" (only `this.flows` is walked); the mount ahead of `/automation/:name`; the UI reader parsing the answer through `RecordUpdateStartsResponseSchema` and drawing nothing on a refusal, a failure, a malformed envelope or an empty list.

Escalations for the adopting seat:
- A security item is with the owner seat.
- The ruling record 7073655354 reads `Metadata-protocol: none`; the shipped declaration is `added` by a seat amendment the gate forced. The substance of the ruling is unchanged, but the PR body's 维护者速读 says nothing needs the maintainer: the seat decides whether a corrected declaration line on a ruled card is his to see.

L1 REWORK · head `99bfd857eb823d672ab57e10b0c7d916d2064a27` · 2026-11-22T10:11Z

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化:列表单元格和记录页里移动阶段时,确认框在原来那句「可能触发相关自动化」下面,列出这次移动会启动的流程名称(按读者语言显示);会发起审批的流程会标出来。服务端新增一个只读接口 `POST /api/v1/automation/_record-starts` 来回答这个问题。
- 为什么做:卡 #35928,按裁决 7073655354:能读这条记录的人可以看到流程名称;钩子一律不列;不新增权限。
- 出错会怎样:接口只预览,不运行任何东西,也不写任何东西。读取失败或什么都没列出时,确认框和以前一样。可以整体撤回。
- 要你做什么:无。
- 席位意见:REWORK,要改 2 项,都不大:一处 PR 正文的声明行,这是 CI 唯一红的原因;以及两条拒绝用例补上 `code` 断言。实现本身我读下来没有问题。

## 要改的(2 项)

1. **PR 正文的 `Metadata-protocol:` 行**。正文写的是 `Metadata-protocol: none`,但 diff 改动了 `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`:三个 RecordUpdateStarts schema 带来 10 个新键。Check Changeset(job 137157633877)因此在这个 head 上失败:「This PR declares … metadata-protocol `none`, and it moves a metadata-protocol baseline」。changeset `35928-record-update-starts-read.md` 自己写的是 `Metadata-protocol: added`,并且把 `@objectstack/spec` 定为 `minor`,这是对的。请把 PR 正文这一行改成和 changeset 一致的 `added`。改正文不会动 head,只需要让 Check Changeset 重跑转绿。
2. **两条拒绝用例只断言了 `status`**(ADR-0112 要求 `code` 和 `status` 都断言):`packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-record-update-starts.test.ts` 里的「refuses an anonymous caller 401 before any read」和「answers 501 on an engine without the preview」。同一个文件里 404、400 那几条都断言了 `code`,请这两条也补上 `body.error.code`,值以这两个入口实际回的为准。

## 席位核对(本轮已读,下一轮增量时只核上面两项加 CI)

- 形态:`l1-face --pr 36316` 只标了 all-checks 一项(Check Changeset failure),其余都是 ok:draft、base `main`、`Fixes #35928`,两份 changeset 覆盖所有受影响的已发布包,`Clause-②: yes (widening)`。改动 60 个文件,+1532 −56;`check-governed-merges` 判定 NOT governed,1588 行。
- 服务端读法:先查 query 集合(不收任何参数),再按 `RecordUpdateStartsRequestSchema` 校验 body;然后以调用者身份走 `/data` 的 `callData get` 读记录,读不到就原样返回那次读的拒绝(读不到和不存在一样回 404);最后才问引擎。引擎只看已启用、已挂在 record_change 触发器上、对象一致、`recordChangeTriggerFiresOnUpdate` 为真的流程,再用每次运行都会经过的那一道 `startConditionHolds` 判断启动条件;条件求值抛错的不列出。是否会发起审批,看流程里有没有 approval 节点。`trigger-record-change` 的 `triggerTypeToHookEvents` 改为调用 spec 的 `recordChangeTriggerHookEvents`,所以触发器实际绑定的事件和预览所依据的是同一套语法。路由账本加了一行,dispatcher 把这个字面路由注册在 `/automation/:name` 之前;地址表在这个字面量上只放行 POST。
- 给 L2 的两点(不改判):① 预览是在调用者读到的记录上求值的,字段级权限会把部分字段遮掉,所以引用了调用者看不到的字段的条件,可能被判成「不启动」。文档已写明「a condition that reads a field the caller cannot see is judged here on what the caller sees」,这种偏差只会漏列,不会泄露;② 预览直接遍历引擎的 `flows` 表,和实际触发时的分发用的是同一份;多组织部署下这里是否需要按组织筛选,我没有单独核实,请契约档的 L2 一并判断。
- 文档逐句核:`flows.mdx` 新增一节,`plugin-grid.mdx` 改了确认框一句,`references` 里的计数 1708→1711、521→524 加上新的三个 schema 名,和 diff 都一致。「匿名调用回 401」由域级的匿名兜底给出,有用例钉住,只是缺了 `code`,见第 2 项。
- UI:`useRecordUpdateStarts` 每次待定的移动只问一次,答案按 key 对应,所以不会显示上一次移动的流程;请求失败或没列出流程时什么都不画。`StageChangeStarts` 用 `activeFlowsBundle` 加 `translateFlow` 显示流程名,和流程运行器的做法一样;`flowsBundle` 从 app-shell 的内部 util 挪进了 `@object-ui/i18n`,两处调用方已经跟着改了。
- nit:「is not read as a flow name」那条只断言了引擎没被调用,没有断言 GET 实际回了什么。
- 门禁 check-runs @ `99bfd857`:64 success · 13 expected skip · **1 failed(Check Changeset)**。
- 落地条款:非受管;两项改完、CI 全绿后做增量 L1,再加席位契约档 L2 PASS,之后由区 ready + auto-merge。

L1 REWORK(增量)· head `d2279e6cc647e310bf98c7aa2b98498acea8db96` · 2026-11-22T12:01Z

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化:和上一轮一样:移动阶段时,确认框会列出这次移动会启动的流程名称。这一轮服务端那个只读接口多了两种拒绝:提议修改的键不是对象上声明过的字段,回 `400`;读不到记录,回 `404`。
- 为什么做:卡 #35928。这一轮是对我的 REWORK 7077634116 和席位契约档 L2 的修改。
- 出错会怎样:最坏情况是确认框里少列几个流程,不会运行或写入任何东西。可以整体撤回。
- 要你做什么:无。
- 席位意见:REWORK,共 2 项,都只改测试和 changeset。我上一轮的第 1 项已经改好;第 2 项还没改。
